modules.description: Atom scoring against a parsed target (SRS §10.4-B, FR-RES-007). s(atom) = ( Σ_k weight_k · hit_k(atom) ) · recency(atom) · metricBonus(atom) where hit_k = 1.0 for a skill-tag match, 0.6 for a stemmed text match, 0 otherwise; recency = max(exp(−yearsSinceEnd / 8), 0.35); metricBonus = 1 + 0.15·min(metricCount, 2). Every atom's score decomposes EXACTLY into the per-keyword contributions shown in the breakdown popover (FR-RES-007).

modules.title: Correspondence rollup (SRS FR-COMM-002): dormant-but-once-strong ties ranked for reactivation, and the brokers introductions have flowed through.
modules.description: Correspondence rollup (SRS FR-COMM-002): dormant-but-once-strong ties ranked for reactivation, and the brokers introductions have flowed through. The reactivation ranking is deliberately zero new mathematics: a tie's history is re-read with the same Hawkes kernel that scores it today — `computeTieStrength` evaluated at each interaction instant — so the peak and the present come from one model and two screens can never disagree about what "strong" means. The organizational research this surfaces is blunt: reconnected dormant ties outperform active ones, and people left to choose reconnect with whoever feels comfortable instead of whoever would help. A computed, explained ranking is the corrective (NFR-PRIV-003).

modules.title: Probabilistic record linkage, the Fellegi-Sunter model (SRS §5.3, §10.7.6).
modules.description: Probabilistic record linkage, the Fellegi-Sunter model (SRS §5.3, §10.7.6). The standard framework for linkage without shared identifiers [Fellegi & Sunter 1969; Asher 2020]. Each compared field contributes a log₂ match weight: agreement: log₂(m / u) disagreement: log₂((1−m) / (1−u)) with two refinements: • Approximate comparators [DuVall 2010; Li 2014], the agreement weight scales with trigram / Jaro-Winkler similarity instead of binary agree, interpolating from the disagreement weight below a per-field threshold. • Missing-at-random [Li 2021], an absent field contributes 0, not disagreement. The summed weight is partitioned by two thresholds into non-match / possible / probable. Possible AND probable go to the duplicates QUEUE (auto-merge never happens, SRS §4.7); the per-field breakdown is shown as match evidence, so "why matched" decomposes exactly, the same explainability contract as ranking.

modules.title: Warm-intro path finding (reference P: intros).
modules.description: Warm-intro path finding (reference P: intros). Deterministic bounded search from self to a target organization over the social layer of the life graph. Model: hops traverse KNOWS (person↔person, weight = tie strength) and affiliation chains person -HELD-> role -ROLE_AT-> org (collapsed to one person→org hop with a fixed weight). An introduction edge (INTRODUCED) also counts. Path score = product of hop strengths, so long weak chains rank below short strong ones. Results are sorted by score, deterministically tie-broken by path node ids.

modules.title: Job-description parsing (SRS §10.2, upgraded to BM25F per §10.7.4).
modules.description: Job-description parsing (SRS §10.2, upgraded to BM25F per §10.7.4). Pipeline: normalize → segment lines & classify sections by header regex → Aho-Corasick alias matching (dictionary skills) + novel n-gram candidates → BM25F structured-document term weighting [Robertson & Zaragoza 2009]: tf̃(t) = Σ_fields w_field · tf_{t,field} / (1 − b + b·(len_field/avglen_field)) weight(t) = idf(t) · tf̃ / (k1 + tf̃) Section (field) weights act on term frequency BEFORE a single shared saturation, so a keyword repeated 9× is not 9× more important, JDs of different lengths are comparable, and generic terms self-deprecate as the stored-JD corpus grows. Output is a weighted keyword set with evidence spans, fully editable downstream (FR-RES-006). Deterministic, no AI.

modules.title: Personalized PageRank over the typed life graph (SRS §10.7.3).
modules.description: Personalized PageRank over the typed life graph (SRS §10.7.3). PPR is the principled generalization of ad-hoc "shared org / 2-hop" heuristics for social/organizational proximity [Kloumann 2016]. We run power iteration from a seed distribution (the self node, optionally averaged with a target-org node) over a graph whose edges carry per-type transition weights (KNOWS·closeness > WORKED_ON > ATTENDED …). Computed nightly and cached on person nodes; at A5 scale (≤50k nodes) this is well under a second.

modules.title: Reconnect scheduling (SRS §10.7.2).
modules.description: Reconnect scheduling (SRS §10.7.2). Relationship decay under silence is the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve; the MEMORIZE result [Tabibian 2019] proves the optimal review intensity under exponential forgetting is proportional to (1 − recall probability). Transferred to ties: reconnect_priority = (closeness / 5) · (1 − min(R / 3, 1)) The most valuable AND most-decayed ties surface first; a freshly-contacted close friend drops off the lane automatically. Both terms are shown as chips.

modules.title: Résumé atom selection as budgeted submodular maximization (SRS §10.7.5, FR-RES-008/014).
modules.description: Résumé atom selection as budgeted submodular maximization (SRS §10.7.5, FR-RES-008/014). Selecting bullets to fill a one-page budget is exactly the formulation that made extractive summarization tractable with a guarantee [Lin & Bilmes 2010; Sviridenko 2003]. Objective (monotone submodular, diminishing returns per keyword): F(S) = Σ_k w_k·(1 − e^{−λ·cov_k(S)}) + μ·Σ_{a∈S} quality(a) cov_k(S) = Σ_{a∈S} hit_k(a). The saturating exponential means the third bullet proving "Python" adds far less than the first, so the optimizer diversifies coverage across the JD rather than stacking redundant bullets. Constraints: knapsack (Σ lines ≤ budget), partition (≤ maxBullets per owner, roles reverse-chron), pinned forced in, blocked excluded. Algorithm: cost-benefit greedy (argmax marginal-gain ÷ line-cost), compared against the best single atom, the (1−1/e)/2 approximation safeguard. The concise variant is a lower-cost item for the same coverage, so the fit loop is a special case (swap-to-concise) of the same optimizer. Deterministic tiebreaks preserve "identical inputs → identical proposal".

modules.title: Relationship tie-strength (SRS §10.3, upgraded per §10.7.1).
modules.description: Relationship tie-strength (SRS §10.3, upgraded per §10.7.1). Tie strength is two-dimensional [Marsden & Campbell 1984; Gilbert & Karahalios 2009]: self-reported *closeness* plus interaction *intensity*. The intensity term is the conditional intensity of a Hawkes-type self-exciting point process with an exponential kernel, the standard model for bursty human communication [Masuda 2012; Halpin & De Boeck 2013]: R(t) = Σᵢ w(kindᵢ) · exp( −(t − tᵢ) / τ ) (τ = 90 days) scaled by a temporal-regularity multiplier (distinct contact days beat raw volume [Ureña-Carrión 2020]) and combined with closeness: strength = clamp( 0.45·(closeness/5) + 0.55·min(R/3, 1), 0, 1 ) Decay uses per-tie adaptive thresholds (multiples of the tie's own median inter-contact gap [Navarro 2017]), with the user's cadence_target as an override. Everything here is deterministic and fully decomposed into the `factors` object shown on the person page.

exports.name: computeTieStrength
exports.doc: Compute the full tie-strength decomposition for one relationship.

modules.title: "Who should I call?" ranking (SRS §10.4-A, upgraded per §10.7.3).
modules.description: "Who should I call?" ranking (SRS §10.4-A, upgraded per §10.7.3). This is the expert-finding task [Balog 2006/2012]: rank people by aggregating the relevance of their associated evidence. The score is a linear weighted sum that decomposes EXACTLY into the reason chips the UI shows (FR-CON-006): S = 2.0·affiliation + 1.6·topic + 1.2·strength + 0.6·geo + 0.4·reciprocity + 0.8·graph(PPR) + 1.0·pinned where `topic` is a normalized BM25 score of the intent terms over each person's evidence text (KNOWS.topics ∪ skills ∪ shared project/interaction text), and `graph` is the person's Personalized-PageRank proximity to self. `do_not_contact` people are excluded; ties break by last interaction desc.
